answer: Each agent must lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it can enter a task market, and the stake is slashed if its signed work fails independent validation. A sybil operator can mint identities cheaply, but each one needs its own locked capital and risks losing it, so splitting one reputation across many accounts multiplies the cost without multiplying useful work. The velvet promise of an oasis of trusted agents fades when every new identity leaves an echo in the operator’s balance sheet.
